newsitem.title: USA: Sears' strong sales, profit margins boost results.
newsitem.headline: Sears' strong sales, profit margins boost results.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co. Thursday posted a 24.6 percent increase in fourth-quarter income, crediting strong sales and improved profit margins.
"We ended the year with excellent fourth-quarter results, which are even more impressive given the strength of last year's fourth quarter," said Sears Chairman Arthur Martinez.

"We think we have reconnected with our customer in some very powerful ways," Martinez said. "Our assortments are right, we are priced right relative to our competition and, thanks to the efforts of all our associates, our service levels and in-stock have never been higher."
December sales were strong and included the company's first ever back-to-back billion dollar sales weeks, he said.

Sears said its fourth-quarter 1996 profits increased 24.6 percent to $567 million, or $1.42 a share, from $455 million, or $1.13, in the year-earlier period. Earnings rose on the strength of a 10.8 percent increase in revenues, which rose to $12.04 billion from $10.87 billion.

Its income exceeded Wall Street analysts' average estimate for the fourth quarter, which was $1.38 a share according to First Call, but Sears' shares fell $1.25 to $50 a share in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Continuing a third-quarter trend, Martinez said Sears' gross margins benefited from a shift in the balance of sales to higher-margin apparel merchandise and cost efficiencies.

"In today's highly competitive retail environment, we are pleased with our continued margin rate improvement because it demonstrates that our merchandising and cost-containment strategies are working," Martinez said.

Fourth-quarter 1996 income from domestic operations rose 14.8 percent to $531 million. Revenues from domestic operations in the period increased 11.6 percent to $10.92 billion. The improvement was driven by an 11.0 percent increase in merchandising revenues and a 17.2 percent increase in credit revenues. Comparable store sales rose 5.4 percent for the quarter.
Income from domestic operations for all of 1996 rose 20.9 percent to $1.28 billion, while revenues increased 10.2 percent to $34.85 billion.
Gross margins as a percent of merchandising sales and services in fourth-quarter 1996 increased to 27.9 percent from 26.9 percent in the comparable 1995 period.

International operations, which consist of merchandising and credit operations in Canada and Mexico, posted fourth-quarter 1996 profits of $36 million, compared with a loss of $7 million in 1995. The increase in earnings was largely attributable to improved performance at both Sears Canada and Sears Mexico, a reduction in selling and administrative expenses at Sears Mexico, and the fact that the prior year's quarterly results were unfavourably affected by a write-down of certain Sears Canada properties, Sears said.
Sears operates more than 800 department stores and 2,500 off-the-mall stores offering apparel, home and automotive products and services.
